newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon delays TI deal for two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon delays TI deal for two weeks.

text.p: Raytheon Co said Tuesday it had reached agreement with the Justice Department to delay its proposed $2.95 billion purchase of Texas Instruments Inc's defense business for two weeks to June 30.
The two-week delay will give the Justice Department more time to examine the proposed takeover, Raytheon spokesman Robert McWade said.
"Both sides agreed mutually to take another two weeks to finalize the process," he said. "We're making progress. There's only one issue left."

A source close to the deal said the Justice Department is examining how the merger would strengthen Raytheon's hand in monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) used in high-technology military applications such as aircraft and other weapons sytems. MMICs are a very small part of the overall deal, the source said.
When asked about MMICs, McWade said that "there is substantial competition" in the market.
"Right now, today, there are nine defense companies capable of manufacturing the high-quality MMICs in question," he said.
McWade said Raytheon's proposed $9.5 billion takeover of Hughes Electronics Corp's defense business is still expected to close in the fall.
